title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(垂水弘夫研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Tarumi Hiroo)
keywords: Thermal environment 2.Green building 3.Energy conservation 4.Air conditioning system 5.Natural power sources
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn about human thermal environments. (2) learn about energy conservation and green buildings. (3) learn about radiation cooling/heating systems for zero-energy buildings. (4) learn about natural power sources in buildings’ surroundings.
advice: Buildings and residences have entered a time when energy conservation is called for. As well as securing the health and comfort of users or residents, buildings and residences are beginning to make energy themselves, and there is a need to realize net-zero energy conditions. In Project Design III at the Tarumi laboratory, students will be doing research on the use of natural energy power. There are various kinds of natural power sources in buildings’ surroundings, such as sunshine, rain, wind, clouds, green, the ground, and water. The planned subjects of research are as follows: 1. Experimental studies on the ceiling radiation of cooling/heating systems using groundwater. 2. Monitoring of the thermal effect of a heating/cooling trench. 3. Research on the thermal effect of a system that indirectly uses subterranean heat by installing a ventilation duct in a heating/cooling trench. 4. Research using numerical analysis methods to estimate the thermal effect of a heating/cooling trench through subterranean heat transfer. 5. Research on the effect of groundwater application on the summer thermal environment on agricultural greenhouses. 6. Monitoring of subterranean thermal effects in an earth tube residence. 7. Study on net-zero energy buildings and campuses.
requiredKnowledge: Students must have acquired credits for Building Equipment and Environmental Design for Architecture I.

activityGoals.body: Students can review previous research relevant to a project theme.
Students can conceive an experiment, survey, and analysis necessary to move the research forward.
Students can correctly explain actual conditions and phenomena related to the environment & energy consumption.
Students can create and display suitable charts to aid in explanations to third parties.
Students can create an appropriate project report.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Students review previous research relevant to a project theme crossing to two or more scientific fields. (2) Students conceive an experiment, survey, and analysis required to move the research forward and clarify the originality of their research. (3) Students can correctly explain the actual conditions and phenomena related to the thermal environment and primary energy consumption based on usage. (4) Students create and display suitable and attractive charts to the audience in a society presentation. (5) Students create appropriate project reports.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Students review previous research relevant to a project theme. (2) Students conceive an experiment, survey, and analysis required to move the research forward. (3) Students can correctly explain the actual conditions and phenomena related to the environment and energy consumption. (4) Students create and display suitable charts for explaining their findings to a third party. (5) Students create appropriate project reports.
